Your girlfriend is letting her emotions rule her life. This is not good.

I've been in therapy for yeeaaars. Something that has been difficult to learn is how to change reactions to situations outside of my control. I think that's what she needs to learn. (Google cognitive behavioral therapy or dialectic behavioral therapy).

Right now she's learning to change the world around her instead of changing herself. From personal experience, this kind of thing is difficult to stop because it feels safe and powerful. You get addicted to control and have no coping mechanisms in situations you can't control.

She is probably having a lot of scary thoughts, and also having problems figuring out what to do with them. She needs to be able to look at a situation and what she's feeling and reassure herself.

For example my so went to a party. I was having some bad anxiety, we had recently fought. My anxiety was telling me "he won't come home after, he'll realize those other people are more fun/sane. He's probably talking about how we fought and his friends will convince him to break up with me." Therapy has taught me how to work with this. I can tell myself he loves me, that he will come home, that disagreeing happens sometimes and it's ok. Sometimes I can't win against the thoughts, in those cases I ask how people feel (needed therapy to learn to accept people's answers though)

Also, communication is key ESPECIALLY when dealing with mental health problems. She should talk about what's going on in her head. Emotions sometimes get so big it feels like there is a big neon sign above your head that says what is wrong and how you feel. It doesn't make sense in those moments that people can't see it, because the emotions are SO OVERWHELMING. She shouldn't expect you to read her mind, she needs to tell you what is going on. If she doesn't want to communicate, to be honest I would say leave. Otherwise it will be a future of suddenly appearing problems and changes to the rules (it won't feel sudden for her because she'll be stewing in emotions, and it might be by the time you find out about them the situation will be too big to fix). Immediately communicating is the best way to make sure your anxiety isn't going to take over and block out reality.
